chunks: A group, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Muhammad ibn Mihran Al-Karkhi, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'If a man is in the Masjid during Salat and wants to spit,' so he said, 'On his left. And if he is not in Salat, he should not spit facing the Qiblah, and he may spit on his right and his left.'
ai.seo_question: Where should a person spit in the mosque during and outside of prayer?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the etiquette of spitting during prayer, where one spits to the left to avoid facing the Qiblah directly, and outside prayer, where one must avoid spitting directly in front of the Qiblah, preferring the right or left sides. This ruling reflects the broader Shia jurisprudential principle of maintaining respect for the direction of prayer within the sacred space of the mosque, ensuring that bodily discharges do not detract from the sanctity of the area. The hadith underscores the importance of cleanliness (taharah) and decorum (adab) in communal worship spaces.

en.hubeali: A group, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Muhammad Bin Mihran Al Karkhy, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I said to himasws, ‘The man happens to be in the Masjid in the Salāt, so he wants to spit’. So heasws said: ‘On his left. And if he was in other than a Salāt, so he should not spit facing the Qiblah, and he can spit on his right and his left’.
en.sarwar: 12. A group has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Muhammad ibn Mehran al-Karkhiy from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who is in Masjid in Salah (prayer) and wants to spit away. He (the Imam) said, ‘He can do it toward his left and if he is not in Salah (prayer); he must not do so in front of al-Qiblah (al-Ka‘bah) but do so toward his left or right sides.’”
